analysis.title: Call in the Global Specialist (06/11)
key_insights: Buy Shimamura (8227 JP) as a defensive relative long in the current sell-off. Almost pure domestic player. Earnings expected to stay firm with high-single-digit % operating profit growth this year and mid-single-digit next year, driven by private-brand merchandise and social media promotions. Committed to a 9% ROE target for 2/27. P/E is 14x 2/28.

Buy Idemitsu (5019 JT) ahead of Q2 earnings next Wednesday. JPM expects Idemitsu and ENEOS to raise full-year guidance meaningfully on higher Asian refining margins, resumed diesel exports to Asia from July, and recovered 2Q refining utilization. Forecasts 2Q FY2026 pretax profit of ¥90.9bn and net profit of ¥53.8bn, and expects a net profit guidance upgrade, a dividend hike (initial guidance ¥36/share) and a share buyback.

NAB (NAB AU) is flagged as a canary in the coal mine for Australia, where the policy rate is at an 18-year high and the central bank must keep raising rates despite weakening growth and labor data. NAB, the most exposed to SME clients, raised collective provision coverage to a sector-leading 1.4%. Its 2H26 capital ratio of 11.87% raises concerns about payout sustainability, and it risks becoming the first Australian bank to cut its dividend.

Short LG Energy Solution (373220 KS). After 3Q results, the JPM analyst cut FY26/27 EPS estimates on a 3Q26 non-operating loss of W987bn, higher FY27 interest expense, and lower FY27 China plant and ESS profitability. 4Q26 OP cut to W353bn, 36% below Bloomberg consensus, with OPM at 3%. FY27E EPS is more than 20% below consensus. Net debt/equity rose from 72% to 82%. The stock trades at 55x 27E P/E and 3.2x P/B.

Buy Rolls Royce into its Q3 IMS on Thursday. At 1250p versus 1500p earlier, the risk of an underwhelming update looks discounted. JPM sees a high likelihood of a beat on FY consensus and expects the company to address its 2028 margin guide, which now looks very conservative. 'Power by the Hour' aftermarket contracts are defensive in a higher oil price environment.

Rolls Royce share price weakness has three drivers per JPM: oil price worries about airline flying hours, disappointing Safran results and GE's slower aftermarket growth guidance (narrowbody-driven, with widebody strong), and selling in 'DC Winner' baskets because the Power Systems unit sells diesel backup engines for data centres. JPM sees no near-term earnings risk in Power Systems and sees US midterms raising demand for behind-the-meter power.

Long AppLovin (APP). JPM's specialist argues the Q3 print resolved the concerns about share loss to Unity, the Q2 revenue miss and eComm scaling. APP is growing faster than Unity in dollar terms. Management described a partially rolled-out next-generation model transition comparable to Axon 2.0. Gaming grew nearly 50% y/y and consumer advertiser spend grew triple digits y/y.

AppLovin valuation: the stock is up about 50% from what the specialist calls an artificially depressed low. Bulls see low-$20s 2027 EPS, so 18x ~$22 implies about $400. Revenue can likely grow 20-30% y/y. The covering research analyst rates it Neutral.

Cautious Vodafone (UW). After a c.35% rally tied to Xavier Niel's involvement, JPM sees near-term risk skewed to the downside. Risks include German broadband pricing, uncertainty over Safaricom and potentially more than €1bn of additional funding needed at OXG. Much of the optimism on corporate change appears priced in.

Buy Tokyo Electron (8035 JP / TELWY US). F2Q operating profit beat the buyside bar of ¥261.1bn and FY3/27 OP guidance was raised to ¥1.169trn versus the investor survey's ¥1.066trn. Order wins span mask etch, NAND, film deposition, single-wafer CVD, advanced packaging ALD, advanced logic probers (+60% y/y) and CPO optical engine orders. A F4Q 50% gross margin is achievable if wafer starts are pulled in. A new etch plant opens in Aug 2027.

Tokyo Electron catalysts: monthly October sales from Taiwan customers such as TSMC and ASE, further order win announcements, and Semicon Japan into December where management may update on order wins and capacity.

ICG (UK specialist): cautious on the underlying credit market and fee-related earnings (FRE) valuation. Hyperscaler issuance of high-quality debt, with Google or Microsoft 10-year bonds yielding above 6%, should push required returns higher further down the ratings scale. Fitch's private-credit default rate reached 6.3% in Q3, PIK usage by BDCs is 8% of income versus 5.5% in 2021, and software is 16% of CLO collateral.

ICG valuation: consensus FY28 fee-related earnings of £344m are below FY26's £350m despite projected 14% fee-earning AUM growth. ICG is a meaningful weight in the JPM Momentum Losers basket and has outperformed by 11% in the last month. The shares trade at 18x fee-related earnings, which the author says discounts little risk to flows or fees.

market_movers.rationale: Shimamura (8227 JP) is a defensive relative long in a sell-off with firm earnings. The research analyst is Neutral with a Y3,600 PT based on 15x P/E. No US listing.
Idemitsu Kosan (5019 JT): the specialist expects a net profit guidance upgrade, dividend hike and share buyback with Q2 results. The research analyst is Neutral but bullish into the print.
National Australia Bank (NAB AU): high provisioning, weak capital ratio of 11.87% and risk of a dividend cut. The research analyst is Neutral.
LG Energy Solution (373220 KS) short: 4Q26 OP 36% below consensus, FY27E EPS more than 20% below consensus, and net debt/equity rising to 82%. The research analyst is Neutral with a W380K PT.

Rolls Royce: buy into Thursday's Q3 IMS, with a likely beat versus FY consensus and a possible update to the conservative 2028 margin guide. The research analyst is Overweight. LSE-listed, no clean US ticker.
The TMT specialist is long after the Q3 print resolved the Unity share-loss, algo hiccup and eComm concerns. The research analyst is Neutral. About $400 is implied at 18x ~$22 2027 EPS.
Vodafone: after a c.35% rally on Xavier Niel's involvement, risks include German broadband pricing, Safaricom and more than €1bn of OXG funding. The research analyst is Underweight.
Tokyo Electron: F2Q OP beat the buyside bar and FY3/27 OP guidance was raised to ¥1.169trn, above the investor survey. Order momentum is broad across etch, packaging and logic.
ICG (UK): cautious on credit market deterioration and FRE valuation at 18x. The research analyst's rating is suspended.

sector_views.rationale: Rising Asian refining margins, recovered utilization and resumed diesel and jet exports support upward guidance revisions at Idemitsu and ENEOS.
Rates are still rising despite weakening growth, provisions are building and a credit cycle debate is beginning. NAB is the most exposed.
Tokyo Electron's raised guidance and broad order wins signal strong demand and capacity expansion.
Rising defaults, PIK usage and software exposure in CLOs, plus higher hyperscaler debt yields, pressure the sector.

earnings_insights: Idemitsu Kosan (5019 JT): JPM forecasts 2Q FY2026 pretax profit of ¥90.9bn and net profit of ¥53.8bn (JPM estimates, not yet reported). 1Q reported pretax profit was ¥156.1bn and net profit ¥103.5bn. IFRS adoption from FY2026 prevents y/y comparison. Reports Q2 next Wednesday along with ENEOS.

LG Energy Solution (373220 KS): after 3Q26 results, the JPM analyst cut FY26/27 EPS estimates. Reported 3Q26 non-operating loss was W987bn. The analyst's 4Q26 OP estimate is W353bn, 36% below Bloomberg consensus, with OPM of 3%. FY27E EPS is more than 20% below consensus.

Tokyo Electron: F2Q reported operating profit beat the buyside bar of ¥261.1bn. FY3/27 OP guidance was raised to ¥1.169trn versus the investor survey figure of ¥1.066trn. F4Q gross margin could reach 50% per the JPM analyst's model if wafer starts are pulled in.

AppLovin: Q3 2026 results (reported) addressed prior concerns. Gaming grew nearly 50% y/y, and consumer advertiser spend grew double digits q/q and triple digits y/y. The Q2 2026 revenue miss is characterised as a hiccup. Bulls see low-$20s 2027 EPS, and the author's illustration uses about $22.

Rolls Royce reports its Q3 IMS on Thursday. JPM expects a beat versus FY consensus and a possible update to the 2028 margin guide. Read-across: Safran's results were disappointing, and GE flagged slower aftermarket growth next year on narrowbody exposure while widebody is strong.
NAB (reported this week): collective provision coverage was raised to a sector-leading 1.4%. The 2H26 capital ratio was 11.87%.
ICG: consensus FY28 fee-related earnings of £344m are below FY26's £350m despite 14% projected fee-earning AUM growth. Structured capital and secondaries realisations halved in FY26.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The RBA has kept raising rates against weakening growth and labor-market conditions. The impact of the last two hikes has yet to reach the economy, so a credit cycle debate is beginning.
Rising private-credit defaults, partly restructured into non-accruing loans or PIKs, raise the risk to alternative lenders.

macro_indicators.indicator: PIK usage by BDCs as share of income (Moody's)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Deferred interest is rising, which can hide credit stress in reported income.
High-quality corporate yields at this level should lift required returns for junk and mezzanine debt.

risk_factors: NAB: SME-heavy book, weak 11.87% capital ratio, sustainability of payouts and the risk of the first dividend cut among Australian banks.

LG Energy Solution: higher FY27 interest expense, lower China plant and ESS profitability, margin pressure from FX and ASP, and higher cost-sharing with customers after China's consumption-tax change.
Rolls Royce: high oil prices and airline flying hours, slower aftermarket growth, and selling pressure in data-centre baskets.
Vodafone: German broadband pricing, Safaricom uncertainty and over €1bn of potential additional funding at OXG.
Private credit: Fitch's 6.3% default rate, growing PIK usage, weaker realisations and software exposure in CLO collateral.
Shimamura: warm weather weighing on apparel sales.
vol_and_positioning: Short interest: Shimamura 0.9 days to cover (0.53% of free float), Idemitsu 0.7 days (0.43%), NAB 15.2 days (2.5%), LG Energy Solution 11.7 days (14.3%), Rolls Royce 5 days (2%), AppLovin 2 days (4%), Vodafone 14 days (7%), Tokyo Electron 0.5 days (0.3%), ICG 6.6% of free float (11 days).
Vodafone has just come off a Xavier Niel-led squeeze, with a c.35% rally.
'DC Winner' baskets have been sold off aggressively, hitting Rolls Royce.
ICG is a meaningful weight in the JPM Momentum Losers basket despite an 11% outperformance in the last month.
geopolitical: Higher oil prices are weighing on airline flying-hour expectations and supporting refining margins, as discussed in the Rolls Royce and Idemitsu sections.
China's consumption-tax policy change raises cost-sharing for small-battery makers, per the LG Energy Solution note.
US midterms ('Blue-nami') are expected to increase demand for behind-the-meter power solutions.
cross_bank_references: Third-party research providers published intra-quarter channel checks on AppLovin share loss that were 'frankly wrong' (JPM TMT specialist's view).
